vars.title: Your first script
vars.goal: A folder ~/megalab/pyle with a vars.py file that prints a name and a room number that changes.
steps: In Terminal, make the folder with `mkdir -p ~/megalab/pyle` and go into it with `cd ~/megalab/pyle`.
In VS Code, create the file ~/megalab/pyle/vars.py.
Make a box `name` holding "Ada" and a box `room` holding 4.
Print the name with the label "Name:", then print "Room" and the room number.
Add 1 to room (right side first), then print "Room" and the room number again.
Save, then run it in Terminal: `python3 vars.py`.
hints: Commas in print add one space: `print("Room", room)`.
`room = room + 1` takes room, adds 1, puts it back.

numbers.title: Laptop boxes
numbers.goal: numbers.py works out how 17 laptops fit into boxes of 5.
steps: Create ~/megalab/pyle/numbers.py.
Store 17 in `laptops` and 5 in `per_box`.
Print laptops divided by per_box with `/`.
Print how many FULL boxes you get, then how many laptops are left over.
Print 2 to the power 10.
Run it: `cd ~/megalab/pyle` then `python3 numbers.py`.

types.title: Text to number
types.goal: types.py turns the text "29" into a real number and uses it.
steps: Create ~/megalab/pyle/types.py.
Store the TEXT "29" (with quotes) in `age_text` and print its type.
Convert it to a whole number, store it in `age`, and print age + 1.
Print "Next year: " glued with + to age + 1.
Run `python3 types.py` from ~/megalab/pyle.
hints: `int(...)` turns text into a whole number.
Text + number crashes: wrap the number in `str(...)` first.

strings.title: Slice an email
strings.goal: strings.py cuts pieces out of the address ada@contoso.com.
steps: Create ~/megalab/pyle/strings.py with `email = "ada@contoso.com"`.
Print the first character and the last character.
Print the first 3 characters (the name part).
Print everything from position 4 to the end (the domain).
Print how many characters the address has.
Run `python3 strings.py`.
hints: The @ sits at position 3, so the domain starts at 4: `email[4:]`.

strtools.title: Clean up a name
strtools.goal: strtools.py turns messy input into a clean email and a tidy team line.
steps: Create ~/megalab/pyle/strtools.py with `raw = "  Bram  "` (spaces on both sides).
Trim the spaces and make it lowercase, store the result in `name`.
Use an f-string to print name followed by @contoso.com.
Split the text "Ada,Bram,Lien" on commas into `team` and print it.
Join team back together with " / " between the names and print it.
Run `python3 strtools.py`.

bools.title: Licence check
bools.goal: bools.py answers True/False questions about licences and MFA.
steps: Create ~/megalab/pyle/bools.py.
Store 5 in `licences` and 7 in `users`. Print whether there are more users than licences.
Store True in `is_admin` and False in `mfa`.
Print: admin AND mfa, then admin OR mfa, then NOT mfa.
Run `python3 bools.py`.
hints: True and False have a capital letter and no quotes.

ifs.title: Disk alarm
ifs.goal: ifs.py prints ok, warning or critical for a disk that is 83% full.
steps: Create ~/megalab/pyle/ifs.py with `used = 83`.
If used is 90 or more, print "critical".
Else, if used is 75 or more, print "warning".
Otherwise print "ok".
Run `python3 ifs.py`, then change used to 95 and to 40 and run again to see the other paths.
hints: Strictest check first: the 90 check goes on top.
Indent the print lines with 4 spaces.

for.title: Count the racks
for.goal: for.py prints rack 1 to 3 and the sum of their numbers.
steps: Create ~/megalab/pyle/for.py.
Make `total = 0` BEFORE the loop.
Loop over the numbers 1, 2, 3 with range. Each lap: print "Rack " with the number, and add the number to total.
AFTER the loop (not indented), print "Total: " with total.
Run `python3 for.py`.

while.title: Retry the connection
while.goal: while.py fakes connection tries: it skips try 2 and stops at try 4.
steps: Create ~/megalab/pyle/while.py with `tries = 0`.
Loop while tries is under 5. First thing in the loop: add 1 to tries.
If tries is 2, skip to the next lap.
If tries is 4, print "connected" and leave the loop.
Otherwise print "try" and the number.
Run `python3 while.py`.
hints: Add 1 at the TOP of the loop, or continue would loop forever.

lists.title: Team list
lists.goal: lists.py builds a team list and some ticket numbers and asks questions about them.
steps: Create ~/megalab/pyle/lists.py with a list `team` of Ada, Bram and Lien.
Add Noor to the end and print the list, then print how many people are in it.
Print whether Bram is in the team.
Make `tickets = [4, 9, 2]`. Print the total and the biggest on one line.
Print a sorted copy of tickets.
Run `python3 lists.py`.
hints: `print(sum(tickets), max(tickets))` uses one comma for the space.

dicts.title: Who works where
dicts.goal: dicts.py links people to departments and looks someone up safely.
steps: Create ~/megalab/pyle/dicts.py with a dict `dept`: Ada is Sales, Bram is IT.
Add Lien with Finance.
Loop over the pairs and print each name and department.
Look up Noor without crashing, with "unknown" as the fallback, and print it.
Run `python3 dicts.py`.
hints: `for name, d in dept.items():` gives both.
dicts.expect:
Ada Sales
Bram IT
Lien Finance
unknown

functions.title: Email maker
functions.goal: functions.py has a make_email function you can reuse for anyone.
steps: Create ~/megalab/pyle/functions.py.
Define `make_email` with two inputs: `first`, and `domain` with default "contoso.com".
It should RETURN the first name in lowercase, then @, then the domain.
Print make_email for Ada, for Bram, and for Noor with domain "lab.contoso.com".
Run `python3 functions.py`.
hints: Default value in the def line: `domain="contoso.com"`.
Use return, not print, inside the function.

errors.title: Skip the bad value
errors.goal: errors.py adds up numbers from text and skips the one that is not a number.
steps: Create ~/megalab/pyle/errors.py with `values = ["12", "abc", "7"]` and `total = 0`.
First, try `int("abc")` alone and run the file: read the error name on the last line. Then remove that line.
Loop over values. Under try, add int(v) to total.
Catch that error name and print "skip:" with the value.
After the loop, print "Total:" with total. Run `python3 errors.py`.
hints: The crash ends with `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'abc'`.

tuples.title: Rack spot and team overlap
tuples.goal: tuples.py unpacks a fixed rack position and compares two teams with sets.
steps: Create ~/megalab/pyle/tuples.py with a tuple `spot` holding 3 and 12.
Unpack it into `rack` and `slot` and print "Rack 3 slot 12" with an f-string.
Make set `sales` with Ada and Bram, and set `it` with Bram and Noor.
Print who is in both, then who is only in sales.
Remove the repeats from the list Ada, Bram, Ada, Noor, Bram and print it sorted.
Run `python3 tuples.py`.

comps.title: Emails in one line
comps.goal: comps.py builds a whole email list and a filtered name list, each in one line.
steps: Create ~/megalab/pyle/comps.py with `names = ["ada", "bram", "lien", "noor"]`.
In one line, build `emails`: each name followed by @contoso.com. Print it.
In one line, print only the names that are exactly 4 letters long.
Run `python3 comps.py`.
hints: Filter goes at the end: `if len(n) == 4`.

classes.title: A User blueprint
classes.goal: classes.py has a User class with an email method and a disable method.
steps: Create ~/megalab/pyle/classes.py with `class User:`.
In `__init__`, take name and dept, store both on self, and set self.enabled to True.
Add a method `email` that returns the name in lowercase plus @contoso.com.
Add a method `disable` that sets self.enabled to False.
Make Ada in Sales. Print her email and dept, print enabled, call disable, print enabled again.
Run `python3 classes.py`.
hints: Every method gets `self` as the first input.
Call with a dot and brackets: `u.disable()`.

cmdlets.title: Explore a cmdlet
cmdlets.goal: A folder ~/megalab/poshle with explore.ps1 that tells you about Get-Date and cd.
steps: In Terminal: `mkdir -p ~/megalab/poshle` and `cd ~/megalab/poshle`.
In VS Code, create ~/megalab/poshle/explore.ps1.
Write lines that output the Noun of Get-Date, then its Verb.
Add a line that shows what the alias cd really runs.
Add a line that shows the TypeName of 'Ada' by piping it into Get-Member (first entry).
Run it from Terminal: `pwsh ./explore.ps1`.
hints: Brackets first, then the dot: `(Get-Command Get-Date).Verb`.

vars.title: Build a UPN
vars.goal: hello.ps1 builds ada@contoso.com from variables and shows the quote rules.
steps: Create ~/megalab/poshle/hello.ps1.
Store 'Ada' in $first and 'contoso.com' in $domain.
Build $upn: $first in lowercase, then '@', then $domain, glued with +.
Output "User: $first" in double quotes, then the same text in single quotes but with the word Literal.
Output "UPN: $upn", then "Length: " with its length using $( ).
Run `pwsh ./hello.ps1` from ~/megalab/poshle.
hints: Single quotes keep `$first` as plain text.
vars.expect:
User: Ada
Literal: $first
UPN: ada@contoso.com
Length: 15

operators.title: True or False checks
operators.goal: checks.ps1 runs six quick tests on an address, a list and some maths.
steps: Create ~/megalab/poshle/checks.ps1 with $upn = 'bram@contoso.com'.
Test if $upn ends in @contoso.com with a wildcard, then if it starts with bram with a regex.
Test if the list 'Sales','IT' contains 'it'.
Test 'Bram' against 'bram' case-sensitively.
Output 17 remainder 5, then 17 divided by 5 rounded down.
Run `pwsh ./checks.ps1`.

collections.title: Team box
collections.goal: team.ps1 holds a team array, a department hashtable and one user object.
steps: Create ~/megalab/poshle/team.ps1 with $team holding Ada, Bram and Lien.
Add Noor with +=, then output the count and the last name.
Make a hashtable $dept: Ada = Sales, Bram = IT. Add Noor = Helpdesk.
Output Noor's department, using the key in lowercase: 'noor'.
Make a [PSCustomObject] with Name Lien and Dept Finance and output "Lien works in Finance" from its properties.
Run `pwsh ./team.ps1`.
collections.expect:
4
Noor
Helpdesk
Lien works in Finance

pipeline.title: Emails down the pipe
pipeline.goal: emails.ps1 turns names into emails and shows object versus plain value.
steps: Create ~/megalab/poshle/emails.ps1.
Pipe 'Ada','Bram','Lien' into ForEach-Object and output each name in lowercase followed by @contoso.com.
Make $o = a [PSCustomObject] with Name 'Noor'.
Pipe $o into Select-Object Name, store it in $a and output "[$a]".
Do the same with -ExpandProperty Name into $b and output "[$b]".
Run `pwsh ./emails.ps1` and compare the last two lines.

where.title: Find active Sales users
where.goal: filter.ps1 keeps only the users that match your tests.
steps: Create ~/megalab/poshle/filter.ps1 with an array $users of four [PSCustomObject]s with Name, Dept, Enabled: Ada Sales $true, Bram IT $true, Lien Sales $false, Noor Sales $true.
Output the text 'Active Sales:'.
Keep users whose Dept is Sales AND who are Enabled, and output only their names.
Output 'Disabled:', then use the short Where-Object syntax to keep Enabled -eq $false and output the name.
Run `pwsh ./filter.ps1`.
where.expect:
Active Sales:
Ada
Noor
Disabled:
Lien

shape.title: Ticket stats
shape.goal: stats.ps1 finds the busiest person, the total tickets and a count per department.
steps: Create ~/megalab/poshle/stats.ps1 with $users: Ada IT 4, Bram Sales 9, Lien IT 2, Noor IT 6 (Name, Dept, Tickets).
Sort by Tickets from big to small, keep the first one's Name, and output "Top: ...".
Add up all Tickets with Measure-Object and output "Total tickets: ...".
Group by Dept and output each group as "Name: Count".
Run `pwsh ./stats.ps1`.
hints: After Group-Object, pipe into ForEach-Object and use `$_.Name` and `$_.Count`.
shape.expect:
Top: Bram
Total tickets: 21
IT: 3
Sales: 1

output.title: Round-trip a CSV
output.goal: csv.ps1 saves users to users.csv, shows the file, and reads it back as objects.
steps: Create ~/megalab/poshle/csv.ps1 with $users: two [PSCustomObject]s, Ada Sales and Bram IT (Name, Dept).
Export them to users.csv.
Show the raw file with Get-Content.
Import users.csv into $rows and output "Rows: " with the count.
Output only the Name of the row whose Dept is IT.
Run `pwsh ./csv.ps1`, then open users.csv in VS Code to see it.
hints: Short Where-Object syntax works here: `Where-Object Dept -eq 'IT'`.

ifs.title: Guest or internal
ifs.goal: check.ps1 makes three decisions: guest or internal, manager or not, disk level.
steps: Create ~/megalab/poshle/check.ps1 with $upn = 'noor@fabrikam.com'.
Use switch -Wildcard: *@contoso.com gives 'internal', default gives 'guest'.
Set $mgr = $null and output 'no manager' when it is empty ($null on the LEFT).
Set $used = 83: 90 or more 'critical', elseif 75 or more 'warning', else 'ok'.
Run `pwsh ./check.ps1`. Then change $upn to ada@contoso.com and run again.
ifs.expect:
guest
no manager
warning
(second run: internal on the first line)

loops.title: Loop the team
loops.goal: loops.ps1 makes emails for everyone except Lien and collects rack labels.
steps: Create ~/megalab/poshle/loops.ps1 with $names = 'Ada','Bram','Lien','Noor'.
foreach name: skip Lien with continue, otherwise output the lowercase name plus @contoso.com.
Make $out = @(). With a for loop from 1 to 3, add "Rack $i" to $out.
Output "Racks: " with $out.Count.
Run `pwsh ./loops.ps1`.

functions.title: Your own New-Upn
functions.goal: upn.ps1 has a New-Upn function with a required name, a default domain and an -Upper switch.
steps: Create ~/megalab/poshle/upn.ps1.
Write function New-Upn with param(): a mandatory [string]$First, [string]$Domain defaulting to 'contoso.com', and a [switch]$Upper.
Build the UPN from $First in lowercase, '@' and $Domain. If $Upper is on, output it in capitals, else as is.
Below the function, call it three times: Ada; Bram with -Domain fabrikam.com; Noor with -Upper.
Run `pwsh ./upn.ps1`. Try calling New-Upn with no -First to see pwsh ask for it.
hints: Define the function ABOVE the calls.

errors.title: Catch and dry-run
errors.goal: safe.ps1 catches a missing file and dry-runs a delete with -WhatIf.
steps: In Terminal, in ~/megalab/poshle, run `touch keep.txt` to make a test file.
Create ~/megalab/poshle/safe.ps1. In try: Get-Item ./missing.txt with -ErrorAction Stop, then output 'found'.
In catch: output 'Error: ' plus the error message. In finally: output 'check done'.
Below that, run Remove-Item on ./keep.txt with -WhatIf.
Run `pwsh ./safe.ps1`, then check with `ls` that keep.txt is still there.
hints: Without -ErrorAction Stop the catch never runs.
errors.expect:
Error: Cannot find path '/Users/<you>/megalab/poshle/missing.txt' because it does not exist.
check done
What if: Performing the operation "Remove File" on target "/Users/<you>/megalab/poshle/keep.txt".
(ls still shows keep.txt)

scripts.title: A real report script
scripts.goal: report.ps1 takes a -Dept input, uses StrictMode and logs itself next to the script.
steps: Create ~/megalab/poshle/report.ps1 with param() at the very top: [string]$Dept defaulting to 'Sales'.
Turn on Set-StrictMode -Version Latest.
Build $log with Join-Path from $PSScriptRoot and 'report.log', and start a transcript to it.
Output "Report for $Dept", then stop the transcript.
Run `pwsh ./report.ps1 -Dept IT`, then open report.log in VS Code.
hints: Nothing may sit above param() except comments and #Requires.
Try a typo like `$Dpet` to see StrictMode stop you.
scripts.expect:
Transcript started, output file is /Users/<you>/megalab/poshle/report.log
Report for IT
Transcript stopped, output file is /Users/<you>/megalab/poshle/report.log

exo.title: Count shared mailboxes
exo.where: VS Code + Terminal · pwsh + your M365 tenant (read-only)
exo.goal: exo.ps1 filters fake mailboxes locally, then counts the real shared mailboxes in your tenant.
steps: Read-only mission: you only run Get-* commands (or -WhatIf) against your tenant, nothing changes. If needed, install the module once: `Install-Module ExchangeOnlineManagement -Scope CurrentUser`.
Create ~/megalab/poshle/exo.ps1. Build $boxes from CSV lines with ConvertFrom-Csv: Name,Type with Ada UserMailbox, Helpdesk SharedMailbox, Bram UserMailbox, Finance SharedMailbox.
Output the names of the SharedMailbox rows, then "Shared: " with how many there are.
Add Connect-ExchangeOnline -UserPrincipalName with your own admin account.

Get only shared mailboxes with Get-EXOMailbox -RecipientTypeDetails SharedMailbox -ResultSize Unlimited and output "Tenant shared: " with the count. End with Disconnect-ExchangeOnline -Confirm:$false.
Run `pwsh ./exo.ps1` and sign in when the browser asks.
hints: Wrap the Get in brackets to count it: `(Get-EXOMailbox ...).Count`.
exo.expect:
Helpdesk
Finance
Shared: 2
(the Exchange connect banner)
Tenant shared: <the number of shared mailboxes in your tenant>

mailbox.title: Read the addresses
mailbox.where: VS Code + Terminal · pwsh + your M365 tenant (read-only)
mailbox.goal: mailbox.ps1 tells primary from alias addresses, then reads your own mailbox and dry-runs a change.
steps: Read-only mission: you only run Get-* commands (or -WhatIf) against your tenant, nothing changes. The only Set- command runs with -WhatIf on your own test account.
Create ~/megalab/poshle/mailbox.ps1 with $a = 'SMTP:ada@contoso.com','smtp:ada@contoso.onmicrosoft.com','smtp:ada.v@contoso.com'.
foreach address: if it case-sensitively matches SMTP:* output "Primary: " plus it, else "Alias: " plus it.
Connect-ExchangeOnline, then read your own mailbox with Get-EXOMailbox -Identity <your test UPN> -Properties EmailAddresses and output its EmailAddresses.
Run Set-Mailbox -Identity <your test UPN> -CustomAttribute1 Lab -WhatIf, then Disconnect-ExchangeOnline -Confirm:$false.
Run `pwsh ./mailbox.ps1`.
hints: `| Select-Object -ExpandProperty EmailAddresses` gives the plain list.
mailbox.expect:
Primary: SMTP:ada@contoso.com
Alias: smtp:ada@contoso.onmicrosoft.com
Alias: smtp:ada.v@contoso.com
(your own SMTP:/smtp: addresses, one per line)
What if: (a line saying it would set the mailbox; nothing is changed)

groups.title: Group diff plan
groups.where: VS Code + Terminal · pwsh + your M365 tenant (read-only)
groups.goal: groups.ps1 compares who is in a group with who should be, and dry-runs the fix.
steps: Read-only mission: you only run Get-* commands (or -WhatIf) against your tenant, nothing changes. Membership changes only run with -WhatIf, on a test group.
Create ~/megalab/poshle/groups.ps1 with $now = 'Ada','Bram','Noor' and $want = 'Ada','Bram','Lien'.
Store Compare-Object $now $want in $d.
Output "Add: " for each => item, then "Remove: " for each <= item.
Connect-ExchangeOnline, list the PrimarySmtpAddress of every member of a test distribution group with -ResultSize Unlimited.
Run Add-DistributionGroupMember on that group with your own UPN and -WhatIf, then disconnect. Run `pwsh ./groups.ps1`.
groups.expect:
Add: Lien
Remove: Noor
(the members' addresses, one per line)
What if: (a line saying it would add you; nothing is changed)

graph.title: Read users with Graph
graph.where: VS Code + Terminal · pwsh + your M365 tenant (read-only)
graph.goal: graph.ps1 finds disabled users in fake data, then reads your own user and counts disabled users in the tenant.
steps: Read-only mission: you only run Get-* commands (or -WhatIf) against your tenant, nothing changes. Connect with only the read scope User.Read.All. If needed: `Install-Module Microsoft.Graph.Users -Scope CurrentUser`.
Create ~/megalab/poshle/graph.ps1. Build fake users with ConvertFrom-Csv: Name,Enabled with Ada true, Lien false, Noor true. Output "Disabled: " plus the Name where Enabled is 'false'.
Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'User.Read.All', then output (Get-MgContext).Account.
Get your own user with -UserId <your UPN> -Property DisplayName,Department and Select-Object those two.
Count disabled tenant users with the OData filter accountEnabled eq false and -All, output "Disabled in tenant: " plus the count.
End the script with Disconnect-MgGraph, run `pwsh ./graph.ps1` and sign in.
hints: CSV values are text: compare with `'false'`, not `$false`.
OData has no dash: `'accountEnabled eq false'`.
graph.expect:
Disabled: Lien
<your admin account>
(a small table with your DisplayName and Department)
Disabled in tenant: <a number>

offboard.title: Offboarding dry run
offboard.where: VS Code + Terminal · pwsh + your M365 tenant (read-only)
offboard.goal: offboard-test.ps1 plans an offboarding from a CSV and dry-runs every step on your test account, with a log.
steps: Read-only mission: you only run Get-* commands (or -WhatIf) against your tenant, nothing changes. Every tenant command in this script carries -WhatIf and targets only your own test account.
Create ~/megalab/poshle/offboard-test.ps1. Start a transcript to offboard-test.log next to the script.
Build $rows from 'UPN','ada@contoso.com','bram@contoso.com' with ConvertFrom-Csv. Output "Users: " with the count.
foreach row, output "Block sign-in: " and then "Convert to shared: " with the UPN (lock first, tidy after).
Connect to Graph and Exchange, then on your test UPN run Update-MgUser -AccountEnabled:$false -WhatIf and Set-Mailbox -Type Shared -WhatIf.
Stop the transcript, run `pwsh ./offboard-test.ps1`, and read the .log file.
hints: Check the test account afterwards: still enabled, still a user mailbox.
offboard.expect:
Transcript started, output file is /Users/<you>/megalab/poshle/offboard-test.log
Users: 2
Block sign-in: ada@contoso.com
Convert to shared: ada@contoso.com
Block sign-in: bram@contoso.com
Convert to shared: bram@contoso.com
(connect banners)
What if: (one line per -WhatIf command; nothing is changed)
Transcript stopped, output file is /Users/<you>/megalab/poshle/offboard-test.log
